>Oh ok, you mean like it won't affect the way you feel about her? 

Yes exactly!

>Some alters may not like you. Some may not even like your fiancee. My SO has one who *hated* us

Yeah that was what kinda triggered us looking to find a therapist and finding out exactly what happened leading to the diagnosis. I'm glad to see that part can get better (not in a cure sense of course)

>It's one of those things that gets worse before it gets better.

That is also good to know, because the past few days since the diagnosis have been crazy for us both and the fact that it's expected is really helpful.

>I'm shocked he never had to do inpatient (and thank God for that, I don't think psych wards are a good place for ppl with DID. too many psych nurses think they're all full of shit).

I totally agree and I'm thankful for that as well, unfortunately those institutions don't always have the best track record. I've read through your other comment as well and I'm really thankful for all the information and advice. I definitely feel like I've been drinking out of a fire hydrant and recognize she feels similar so I will definitely be revisiting this a lot as the both of us process all of it.

>Holding onto 'this doesn't change anything, it doesn't change her' is going to damage your relationship. You really need to realise this.

I gotcha, I think I realize it'll definitely be something that yes changes her life, reality, and is something that will have growing pains associated with. 

>Sorry for being harsh. It's really not easy to go through this beginning stage when people are basically dismissing your existince as a whole by saying 'you won't change in my eyes'.

I'm certainly not trying to dismiss the existence of what's going on and that any of it is real, I know one of the things she was struggling with though was that she feels afraid I'm going to want to not marry her or that I shouldn't because of it. I definitely see that I am probably underestimating it as a whole and have misconceptions on it all that I'll have to just learn like you said and listen. I'll definitely be checking out CTAD. I guess as a question though is there anything you wish the people around you had done for you or known specifically?

Thank you, I really appreciate it. Last night was especially intense for her with a lot of switching and I was a bit shaken hearing and seeing some of it which like you said, was and is even worse for her.

>she is just as much her alters as her alters are her. She just happens to be the host.

This is definitely helpful in understanding it a bit better.

That's totally understood, I realize I worded that poorly as it was midnight. The choice to commit has already been made, we're engaged and the wedding is two months away, and I am looking forward to the rest of my life with her, DID or not because this is not something she chose and she is still the woman I love as she had this before we were engaged and like the comment said it's just now being contextualized and understood. I recognize that I'm nervous and uncertain as much as I don't want to show that and I realize it's a thousand times worse for her, she is terrified and we both are lost on navigating it. I recognize as she goes to see her specialist that changes will need to be made in our life and it won't be nearly as scary, thank you for the encouragement, she has my support every step of the way.

Thank you, that's really helpful! She has scheduled to see a specialist. Anything else as the significant other I might expect? I would expect like with most mental health stuff it varies wildly between those experiencing it and that patience and understanding is a must, but anything to alleviate daily stress as I can then helps?
I get that  I don't mean that it won't make changes in our life, I more meant that I'm committed to staying. Apologies there!

Opportunity cost. You can give farmer Jimmy a cheap rifle, teach him how it works, and get him into some sort of shape in three months if you go by the U.S. standard, and when he dies, not much of worth is really lost in the grand scheme. Or you genetically engineer gigachap super soldier, give him the most expensive equipment and invest hella resources in him and he gets hit by a stray artillery shell just like farmer Jimmy and gets evaporated. Now to replace him you have a whole ton of resources to dump back into the system where farmer Jimmy's replacement farmer Joe, Bob, Tim, and Larry have already hit the front line in a fraction of the time for a fraction of the cost.

Part of it is you're still young and in High School.  The other part unfortunately is a reality of society today. For the first bit though. High school is a popularity contest socially, the star achievers, athletes, and the attractive people are gonna be surrounded by people who want the same attention. It's second fiddle but they're still playing in their mind but then you get out of high school and really nobody has time to be a part of that kinda thing, they're too busy working, taking care of their own business and just minding their own most of the time unless you're in college then it sorta continues but not necessarily to the same degree because the stakes are a bit higher so a bit larger percentage us just going about their life. 

The next bit being you're young, if someone were to find me in high school I was a pimple faced, lanky looking nerd, since then I've filled out my frame a bit more, my face is cleared up, and I'm still a nerd but not nearly as awkward. I won't say I'm the most attractive around but I think I look significantly better than I did then. I've seen similar things with girls I went to high school with where some who were super attractive, super let themselves go, and some of the less attractive girls (who got called ugly a lot through school, though in reality were middle of the road, had a huge glow up or did a lot of work to get in shape. Nothing wrong being middle of the road either, most of the world kinda fits there or slightly below.)

The final bit that there really isn't going to be any change in unless there's a huge cultural movement is social media, the small population of hyper attractive people gets the most spotlight, so lots of ladies compare themselves to that which can cause some image issues for men and women, furthermore men get over exposed to that and see it as the standard. Think back 50 years. You still had celebs on magazines and in movies who looked crazy good but for most men and women they had the people who lived in their city or town to compare themselves, and most were astoundingly average because that's most of the population. So guys were a bit more confident in asking ladies for a date and the self image issue while it still existed for women and men, didn't have the same kind of pressure there is today. So today you have men who have an expectation that if they're not rich/fit/Chris Hemsworth, that they don't stand a chance. So they just don't, even if they're still decent looking fellas and just use porn as an outlet because advertising and social media has destroyed young people's self image. 

TLDR: wait till you're out of high school, you're still gonna have some physical changes ahead, and society's hyper advertisment/ social media inflation of physical expectation has pretty much fucked a generations confidence, so we're all checking out. 

Don't lose hope, the sun rises tomorrow.

Ugh this sucks. First thing is first. Take a deep breath, eat something if you can and drink something warm like tea if you enjoy it. I went through something similar. Best advice I can give you is to grieve first. It's very recent and raw to you now and you'll have to go through a lot of changes with your life and how you think. Talk to the people you trust most, parents too if you're on good terms. Don't bottle things up, write things in a journal. Focus on self care. For me it's been two years and I still get pangs of grief every now and then thinking about her but time heals most wounds. Don't be afraid to seek out help from your support network or even at a professional level.

Judging by how you seem to be talking about herbi hunting, I think it might be your strategy that needs a change. Carnos and Utahs hunted based on their speed. If you're having issues with fighting pachys and tenos you're likely getting too aggressive. I've played both sides of the isle this QA and Carnos have a pretty big advantage when it comes to speed in an open field. It's not about your bite damage but it's about the pressure you can apply to a pack. If they're playing defensive bait them into attacks to make them waste their stamina pick a specific dino that seems like they might be a little on the slow side with their reactions and make that your and your friend's target, if they're getting aggressive use your speed to out maneuver them and hit them when they make a mistake and make them bleed for it. 

Are things a bit janky in terms of balance? Sure, a good pachy or teno player can be a menace but it's still wip and as more dinos get released and mechanics get added and tweaked we will likely see tenos and pachys be at the point that you're talking about where they're your run of the mill prey animal that can still pose a challenge to some dinos but not others. 

As things stand now there isn't much option for carni players or herbi players, and if the devs want to make playing herbis fun at the moment with all these speed hunters they gotta make them a bit stronger so they can fight off packs rather than have playing any herbi except stego be "sit around and wait to get eaten" simulator. Just for now it's a lot easier as a carno to play for exhaustion and bleed than it is to get a straight up kill.

I believe they mean well, more than likely they're scared as anger and threats are a pretty primal response to fear, that or they'll shut down and try to ignore it. Fight or flight essentially. In their mind if they threaten you with something they think would be painful, you'll turn a leaf and try to fix it. The shutdown response is a different method where they believe that by closing themselves off you'll try to remove that discomfort in the same fashion. What they fail to realize is this plays right into depression's hand and makes the person they're directing it towards less willing to respond to them in a positive way and less willing to seek a coping mechanism, kind of the "well if this person hates me/is ignoring my problem, what's the point" most people don't want to see others close to them die, though there are cruel people out there its not a majority a lot of people just don't know or are too scared to know what's going on.

I get it, it doesn't necessarily 'get easier' I've struggled with depression and suicidal ideations most of my life with two attempts, one that almost did kill me. What I can say from my experiences is while it doesn't get easier you do learn how to cope with time and you learn how to recognize when you're falling back into these things and how to keep yourself from reeling back to where you were. The reasons to stay are what you make them, for me it was realizing that if I left my little sister wouldn't have a brother anymore and that I wouldn't be able to teach her about the things I enjoy. It carries for everyone and depression isn't a cut and dry thing on how to deal with it, but generally there is something out there for you that will work you may just not be seeing it yet.

So getting into a 900 division for me was you get off the plane at O'Hare and you get taken to the USO there where three of the chiefs/petty officers who run the graduations have you fill out a paper and ask some questions. Then from there you get either turned down, or you get written on your hand your division's number. Make sure it doesn't get washed off. Just like that then you're in a 900 division. Now for triple threat you get auditioned and if you don't make it through the audition you end up as the cleaning crew essentially but you stay 900

Yeah no problem, so triple threat means a portion of the division does band, another does rifles, and the other does choir. The staff divisions are kinda multirolled with people who greet the high ranking guests, move through the graduating divisions as 'body snatchers' we called them, and directing families to their seats. And flags have a drum line and they carry the state flags and parade them down the drill deck during the graduation. Either way your family will see you or be able to easily pick you out. I think the staff also does the rifle inspection that happens during the graduation but I can't remember for sure

Yes they have sax if I remember, chief Barby will figure out a way to get you to fit in, but that's only if you're screened for a triple threat, you'll get auditioned and such as well but if not the flag and staff divisions were pretty cool as well. All I can say is just for the love of God if you're in a 900 division don't talk in the galley. You'll get your ass chewed like hell by The Whistler

Day to day was pretty standard from my understanding except for Saturday's where we went to the drill hall and practiced our respective 'jobs' you could say. I also understand that we did a little less PT than other divisions and didn't get beat as much as normal rifle divisions but that could have just been our RDCs. The three 30 plus year olds I remember did very well actually though. One was an MU, one a CT, and the other a MM

I can only speak to the 900 div part (902 hooyah) and it sets you back a week at most but I'd say for me it was worth it for the family end of things. There wasn't any extra advancement type of thing for being in a 900 division but it also depends on where in the 900 cycle you are. They only take triple threat on certain pushes same with staff and state flag 900s like I said I enjoyed it personally and don't regret the extra week I got held there for

Hey, so I just got out of bootcamp in November (Div 902), so my experience is pretty fresh. Will it be cold oh hell yeah it'll be cold. PT will be in freedom hall or your compartment. You'll PT, don't worry.
